answers.text: List three lines every time, same order: drop-off time, pallet count, and damage noted. Drop-off time as hours and minutes, pallet count is what is actually taken off at that stop, not the whole truck's load, and damage noted is whatever the driver actually says, written down as he says it.

For the follow-up list I would want time, customer, topic, and outcome, in that order every time, that is the main thing. Follow-up calls are important generally, we lose track of people if we do not stay on top of them.

If the crew starts at eight and needs about six hours, would that not already be done the same day, the 22nd, early afternoon? The note says the 23rd though. Something there does not sound right to me.
118 compared to 96 last month, that is a fair jump, roughly what they have put down I think.
I would go with Output 2, seems the more solid one of the two. SLA numbers matter a lot for how the team is judged each quarter, so it is good someone is keeping an eye on it.
I would probably send the first email, it gets straight to the point and does not drag on with numbers.
5. No, that is someone's home address, personal, would not put that anywhere outside HR. For the others I would have to think about it case by case, depends what the tool actually is.

The hourly rates and retainer cap I would keep out of it, would not want those going into something we have not cleared. Clients can be funny about their agreements getting shared around anyway, better to keep the whole thing close.
What I would do is count the stock at each depot myself against what the system shows, before the summary goes over to finance at month end.
Reading the invoice PDF right at the start worries me most, if the AI gets a number wrong there the whole thing that follows is built on that mistake.
